textbook_summary: P waves are replaced by continuous, regular sawtooth F waves without an isoelectric baseline, clearly visible in II, III and aVF.
The atrial rate is 240-350/min, commonly with fixed 2:1 or 4:1 conduction; QRS complexes are usually narrow.
scope: Teaching examples of fixed-ratio and repeating variable-conduction flutter. Electrode amplitudes, F-wave contours, timing and variable sequences are authored choices, not anatomical localization. F waves continuously overlap QRS/T.
limitations: Fixed 300/min examples with 2:1, 3:1 or 4:1 conduction and a repeating 2/3/4 variable sequence. Other variable-conduction and impure-flutter patterns remain unimplemented.
Flutter mechanical contraction is not modeled; normal AtrialMechanical events and the normal CVP a wave are suppressed.
The 2:1 and variable-conduction physiology demos shorten pulse and pressure morphology support to 320 ms while retaining existing ejection and RC parameters; these are not calibrated hemodynamics.
QT is fixed at 300 ms, without beatwise QT feedback or clinical detection.
The 3:1 example has a ventricular rate of 100/min and retains the 160 ms mechanical offset, 80 ms QRS, 300 ms QT and continuous F waves. These do not establish calibrated flutter filling or ejection.

The variable example rejects conflicts with independent ventricular periods, mechanical stride or timed suppression. It is not an AV-node refractory or beatwise filling model; pressure/Pleth use existing teaching parameters for the minimum 400 ms interval.
